easy.def: To glide on ice or the ground with special shoes.
examples: I skate on the ice.
We skated at the rink.
She skates well.

more.def: To glide over ice or smooth ground on wheels or blades attached to your shoes.
examples: We skated on the frozen pond.
She skates around the rink.
The kids skated down the sidewalk.

easy.def: A boot with a blade or wheels on the bottom.
examples: I put on my skates.
My skate is blue.
I tied my skates.

more.def: A shoe with a metal blade or wheels on the bottom for gliding.
examples: She laced up her ice skates.
He wore roller skates on the smooth path.
My skate got stuck in a crack.

related.def: A person who rides a skateboard.

easy.def: A board with wheels that you stand on and ride.
examples: I ride my skateboard.
The skateboard has four wheels.
He fell off his skateboard.

more.def: A short board with four small wheels that you stand on and ride along the ground.
examples: I wore a helmet and knee pads when I rode my skateboard.
He learned to do a trick on his skateboard at the park.
The skateboard rolled down the hill by itself.

easy.def: To ride on a board with wheels.
examples: I skateboard at the park.
He skateboards to school.
They skateboarded all day.

more.def: To ride along on a short board with small wheels.
examples: My cousin skateboards at the park every Saturday.
He skateboarded down the sidewalk, wearing a helmet.
She is learning to skateboard on the smooth, flat path.

easy.def: A person who skates.
examples: The skater glided on the ice.
She is a fast skater.
A skater jumped and spun.

more.def: A person who moves along on ice skates, roller skates or a skateboard.
examples: The skater glided across the frozen pond with her arms out wide.
A group of skaters practiced tricks at the park.
The young skater spun twice in the air and landed smoothly.

easy.def: To run away fast.
examples: Skedaddle!
The kids skedaddled.
The mouse skedaddled.

more.def: To run away quickly, used in casual talk.
examples: The mice skedaddled when the light came on.
The kids skedaddled when the bell rang.
The cat skedaddled out the door.

easy.def: Having to do with bones.
examples: The skeletal system holds you up.
A skeletal hand.
The skeletal model stood.

more.def: Having to do with the skeleton, or very thin, like bones.
examples: The skeletal system holds up the body.
The museum had a skeletal model of a dinosaur.
A skeletal tree stood in the snow.

easy.def: All the bones in a body.
examples: Your skeleton holds you up.
A fish has a skeleton too.
We saw a skeleton in science class.

more.def: The frame of bones that supports the body of a person or animal.
examples: The museum has the skeleton of a huge dinosaur.
The human skeleton has more than two hundred bones.
We found the skeleton of a small bird in the woods.

easy.def: Not sure that something is true.
examples: I am skeptical.
A skeptical look.
She was skeptical.

more.def: Having doubts and not quick to believe that something is true.
examples: I was skeptical when he said he had seen a unicorn.
She gave a skeptical look at the claim.
A good scientist is skeptical and asks for proof.

easy.def: In a doubtful way.
examples: He looked skeptically.
She listened skeptically.
They watched skeptically.

more.def: In a way that shows you doubt something.
examples: He looked skeptically at the tall tale.
She listened skeptically to the story.
The teacher raised an eyebrow skeptically.

easy.def: A quick drawing.
examples: I made a sketch.
The sketch is in pencil.
She drew a sketch of a bird.

more.def: A quick drawing that is not finished in detail.
examples: I made a quick sketch of the dog.
The artist's sketch was done in pencil.
She drew a sketch of the lake.

easy.def: To draw quickly.
examples: I sketch the tree.
She sketched the house.
He sketched a cat.

more.def: To make a quick, rough drawing.
examples: I sketched the old barn in my notebook.
She sketched the view from the window.
He sketched a picture of the horse.

easy.def: A book for drawing.
examples: I draw in my sketchbook.
The sketchbook is full.
She has a sketchbook.

more.def: A book with blank pages for making drawings.
examples: I drew a horse in my sketchbook.
The artist carried a sketchbook everywhere.
The sketchbook was filled with drawings of birds.

easy.def: A long stick to hold food over a fire.
examples: We put marshmallows on a skewer.
The skewer is long.
He held a skewer.

more.def: A long, thin stick of metal or wood used to hold food while it is cooked.
examples: Dad put pieces of vegetables on a skewer.
We toasted marshmallows on a long skewer.
The cook grilled the meat on a skewer.

easy.def: A long, thin board you wear on each foot to slide on snow.
examples: I wear skis in the snow.
My ski is long.
The skis are on the rack.

more.def: One of two long, thin boards that are fastened to boots for sliding over snow.
examples: I strapped my skis onto my boots.
One ski slid away down the hill.
The skis left two tracks in the snow.

easy.def: To slide over snow on long boards.
examples: We ski in winter.
She skied down the hill.
I want to ski.

more.def: To glide over snow on a pair of long, narrow boards.
examples: We ski in the mountains every winter.
She skied down the slope.
He skied across the snowy field.

easy.def: To slide out of control.
examples: The car skidded on the ice.
My bike skidded.
The truck skidded.

more.def: To slide sideways or forward without control, usually on a wet or slippery surface.
examples: The car skidded on the icy road.
My bike skidded on the wet leaves.
The truck skidded to a stop in the snow.

easy.def: A slide that is out of control.
examples: The car went into a skid.
I felt a skid.
The skid was scary.

more.def: A slide of a vehicle out of control on a slippery road.
examples: The car went into a skid on the ice.
I felt the bike go into a skid.
The driver steered out of the skid.

easy.def: A person who skis.
examples: The skier went down the hill.
A skier wears boots.
He is a good skier.

more.def: A person who glides on skis over snow.
examples: The skier sped down the snowy hill.
A skier wears long poles and boots.
She is the best skier in her class.

easy.def: A small, light boat.
examples: We rowed a skiff.
The skiff is small.
A skiff floated by.

more.def: A small, light boat with one or two sails or oars.
examples: The fisherman rowed his skiff to the shore.
A skiff bobbed on the quiet lake.
We climbed into the skiff and pushed off.

easy.def: Sliding over snow on long, thin boards called skis.
examples: I like skiing.
We go skiing in winter.
Skiing is fun in the snow.

more.def: The sport or activity of sliding over snow on skis.
examples: We go skiing in the mountains every winter.
Skiing down the hill was fast and fun.
He took lessons in skiing and learned to stop on the slope.

easy.def: Being able to do something well.
examples: Drawing is a skill.
She has great skill at soccer.
I learned a new skill.

more.def: The ability to do something well, which you get from practice.
examples: Riding a bike takes skill.
She has great skill at playing the piano.
Reading is a skill that gets better with practice.

easy.def: Very good at something.
examples: She is a skilled painter.
A skilled player.
He is skilled at chess.

more.def: Having the training and practice to do something very well.
examples: She is a skilled painter who can mix any color.
A skilled carpenter built the wooden bridge.
He is skilled at chess and rarely loses.

easy.def: A frying pan.
examples: Mom cooked eggs in a skillet.
The skillet is hot.
Dad washed the skillet.

more.def: A heavy frying pan with a long handle, used for cooking on a stove.
examples: Dad fried bacon in an iron skillet.
The skillet sizzled as he poured in the batter.
She cooked pancakes in a large skillet.

easy.def: Very good at doing something.
examples: She is a skillful singer.
A skillful player.
The skillful potter.

more.def: Having or showing great skill.
examples: She is a skillful painter.
The skillful player scored two goals.
The skillful potter shaped the clay.

easy.def: To glide lightly over a surface.
examples: The bird skimmed the water.
I skim stones on the lake.
The boat skims.

more.def: To move lightly over the surface of something, or to read something quickly without looking at every word.
examples: The bird skimmed over the surface of the lake looking for fish.
We skim stones across the pond.
I skimmed the chapter to find the date I needed.

easy.def: The outside covering of your body.
examples: My skin is soft.
The sun can burn your skin.
Wash your skin.

more.def: The outer covering of the body of a person or animal.
examples: Put on sunscreen to protect your skin.
A snake sheds its skin as it grows.
Her skin felt warm in the sun.

easy.def: The outside layer of a fruit.
examples: Peel the skin off the banana.
An apple has red skin.
The potato skin is thin.

more.def: The outer covering of a fruit or vegetable.
examples: Peel the skin off the orange.
The banana skin was brown and soft.
The tomato skin split in the heat.

easy.def: Very thin.
examples: The skinny cat ran.
A skinny branch broke.
The skinny boy grew taller.

more.def: Very thin, with little fat or flesh.
examples: The skinny cat looked hungry.
A skinny branch snapped in the wind.
The skinny puppy needed more food.

easy.def: To move with little jumps.
examples: The kids skip.
She skipped down the path.
I skip rope.

more.def: To move forward with light hops from one foot to the other.
examples: The children skipped down the sidewalk.
She skipped happily to school.
We skip rope at recess.

easy.def: To leave something out.
examples: Skip the hard question.
I skipped a page.
He skipped lunch.

more.def: To leave something out or not do it.
examples: Skip the hard question and come back to it.
I accidentally skipped a page.
He skipped breakfast and ran to the bus.

easy.def: The captain of a small boat.
examples: The skipper steered the boat.
The skipper waved.
Our skipper was kind.

more.def: The captain of a small ship or boat, or the leader of a team.
examples: The skipper steered the fishing boat out to sea.
The skipper called out orders to the crew.
Our team's skipper led us onto the field.

easy.def: Clothing that hangs down from your middle.
examples: She wore a skirt.
The skirt is red.
My skirt has pockets.

more.def: A piece of clothing that hangs from the waist and covers part of the legs.
examples: She wore a blue skirt to school.
The dancer's skirt twirled as she spun.
My skirt has two pockets.

easy.def: A short play.
examples: We did a skit.
The skit was funny.
Our class performed a skit.

more.def: A short, often funny play.
examples: Our class performed a funny skit about a talking dog.
The campers acted out a skit around the fire.
We wrote a skit about a lost hat.

easy.def: To run with quick, light steps.
examples: Mice skitter across the floor.
The crab skittered.
The leaves skittered by.

more.def: To move quickly and lightly across a surface.
examples: Mice skittered across the kitchen floor.
The crab skittered sideways across the sand.
Dry leaves skittered along the sidewalk in the wind.

easy.def: Easily scared or jumpy.
examples: The horse is skittish.
A skittish cat.
The skittish deer ran.

more.def: Easily frightened and quick to jump or run away.
examples: The skittish horse jumped at the noise.
A skittish cat hid under the bed.
The deer was skittish and ran when we moved.

easy.def: A bottle-shaped pin knocked down in a game.
examples: He knocked down a skittle.
The skittle fell.
The skittles stood in a row.

more.def: One of the bottle-shaped pins that players knock down in a bowling game.
examples: He rolled the ball and knocked down all the skittles.
The skittles stood in a neat triangle.
She set up the skittles for another game.

easy.def: To creep around quietly so that no one sees you.
examples: The cat skulked in the dark.
The fox skulked by the barn.
He skulked in the hall.

more.def: To hide or move around quietly and secretly.
examples: The fox skulked around the henhouse.
The boy skulked in the shadows, hoping not to be seen.
The cat skulked under the porch.

easy.def: The bones of the head.
examples: The skull protects the brain.
A skull is made of bone.
The skull is hard.

more.def: The set of bones that forms the head and protects the brain.
examples: Your skull protects your brain.
The museum has a dinosaur skull.
A helmet protects your skull.

easy.def: A black and white animal that sprays a very bad smell.
examples: The skunk sprayed.
I smelled a skunk.
A skunk lives under the porch.

more.def: A small black and white animal that sprays a strong, bad-smelling liquid when it is scared.
examples: The skunk lifted its tail and sprayed a terrible smell.
A skunk has a bold white stripe down its back.
Our dog got sprayed by a skunk and had to take a bath.

easy.def: The space above us where we see clouds and stars.
examples: The sky is blue.
Birds fly in the sky.
Stars are in the sky.

more.def: The space above the Earth that we see when we look up.
examples: The sky turned orange at sunset.
A kite danced in the windy sky.
Stars fill the sky on a clear night.

easy.def: To jump from a plane and fall through the sky with a parachute.
examples: They skydive from a plane.
He skydived.
I want to skydive.

more.def: To jump out of an airplane and fall through the air before opening a parachute.
examples: She skydived from a plane high above the farm.
The team skydived and then opened their parachutes.
Skydivers float down with a big parachute.

easy.def: A small brown bird that sings while flying high.
examples: A skylark sang in the sky.
The skylark flies up high.
I heard a skylark.

more.def: A small brown bird that sings sweetly as it flies high above the fields.
examples: A skylark sang high above the meadow.
The skylark rose higher and higher into the sky.
We heard a skylark singing over the field.

easy.def: A window in the roof.
examples: The skylight lets in sun.
We have a skylight.
Rain tapped the skylight.

more.def: A window set in a roof or ceiling that lets in daylight.
examples: Sunshine poured through the skylight.
Rain tapped on the skylight.
We could see the stars through the skylight.

easy.def: The shape of buildings against the sky.
examples: We saw the skyline.
The city skyline is tall.
The skyline glowed.

more.def: The outline of buildings or hills seen against the sky.
examples: We looked at the city skyline from the boat.
The skyline glowed at sunset.
Tall buildings made a jagged skyline.

easy.def: To rise very fast.
examples: Prices skyrocket.
The kite skyrocketed.
The temperature skyrocketed.

more.def: To rise very quickly and sharply.
examples: Prices skyrocketed when the supply ran low.
The temperature skyrocketed at noon.
Her fame skyrocketed after the concert.

easy.def: A very tall building.
examples: The skyscraper is tall.
We saw a skyscraper.
A skyscraper in the city.

more.def: A very tall building with many floors, usually found in a big city.
examples: The skyscraper was so tall that its top was in the clouds.
We rode the elevator to the top floor of the skyscraper.
New York City has many famous skyscrapers.
